annotations.text:
Carried over from the Windows app: warm neutral base, traffic-light states, red as the product accent, and the light-weight tabular countdown from the shutdown takeover.

Everything structural is iOS: large titles, inset grouped lists, 52pt rows, system toggles.
The one surface with no desktop equivalent. iOS draws this itself via ShieldConfiguration — you get an icon, a title, a subtitle and up to two buttons. Everything here stays inside that budget.
Open question: if shielding uses .all() the app shields itself, and this screen can never be seen. Designed on the assumption we exempt Hard Lock's own token.
No daily-cap screen: the iOS spec drops the cap deliberately, so there is no REMAINING/USED pair to carry over. The cutoff is the whole model.
